text.tspan: EC2 instance types: read the name, pick the family
m = instance class (family) · 5 = generation (higher is newer) · 2xlarge = size inside the class
Size: nano < micro < small < medium < large < xlarge < 2xlarge … (more vCPU, RAM, network)
Suffixes you will see: g = AWS Graviton (ARM), a = AMD, i = Intel, d = local NVMe instance store, n = more network
Exam hook: "R" = RAM (memory), "C" = compute, "I" = I/O (storage), "G"/"P" = graphics/GPU, "T" = turbo/burstable.
There is also an HPC Optimized family (Hpc). Compare all types on instances.vantage.sh (community site, not AWS).
